k.q: Spot the difference between adding character counts and calculating text storage.
k.code:
characters = 2
bytesPerCharacter = 3
sizeBytes = characters + bytesPerCharacter
print(sizeBytes)
p: Predict the incorrect number of bytes.
Explain why character encoding determines the bytes required, even though the CPU executes translated instructions.
k.a: Addition incorrectly prints 5. The correct raw calculation for the explicitly stated three-byte encoding is characters * bytesPerCharacter = 6 bytes. Real encodings such as UTF-8 can use variable bytes per character; the example assumes three bytes for each of these two characters. High-level source still needs suitable translation/execution before CPU machine instructions run.

e: Give one benefit of high-level languages. [2 marks]
More readable and often easier to develop/maintain, or portable with suitable runtimes.
Compare compiler and interpreter at a broad level. [4 marks]
Compiler translates a program to executable/intermediate output; interpreter executes through an interpreting environment.
Explain why machine code depends on processor architecture. [2 marks]
Instructions use a machine-specific instruction set understood by that CPU.

mastery.task: Write a classification algorithm that describes the role of compiler, interpreter and CPU for a chosen code workflow, with an unknown-language input.
mastery.hint: Keep factual distinctions rather than ranking all implementations by speed.
mastery.answer: Compiler produces translated executable/intermediate output, interpreter executes through runtime, CPU runs machine instructions. Unknown input should be handled without false claims.
